edges.effect_quant: Dose-response meta-analyses backed by prospective cohorts suggest a small average effect that is directionally consistent but not dramatic.
edges.mechanism: This factor likely influences Dementia (all-cause) through a mix of reserve, disability, social engagement, inflammation, and shared chronic-disease burden rather than one single biochemical pathway. That matters because some of these variables behave partly as markers of physiologic aging and partly as modifiable contributors.
edges.summary: Dose-response meta-analyses backed by prospective cohorts link hearing aid use to lower risk of dementia (all-cause) in older adults with hearing loss. The average effect is usually small rather than dramatic, so this edge is better read as a risk modifier than a stand-alone cause or cure.
edges.caveats: Dose, timing, and baseline risk still matter. Observational edges may partly reflect broader lifestyle patterning, while small trials can overstate benefit if follow-up is short.
